title: Campus Exchange
subtitle: AI-Powered Campus Marketplace
summary: A verified campus marketplace combining recommendation search, pricing intelligence, expense sharing, and production-ready APIs for safer student transactions.
problem: Students need a trusted place to buy and sell items, split expenses, and avoid scams without depending on fragmented social-media groups.
approach: Designed a Next.js frontend backed by FastAPI services.
Used PostgreSQL with pgvector for semantic and personalized recommendations.
Added Redis for fast access patterns and production-oriented caching.
Structured the product around verified users, price guidance, and practical campus workflows.
role: Founder and lead developer - product architecture, AI features, backend services, data layer, and deployment decisions.
results: Reported a 15% gain in pricing accuracy.
Delivered a full-stack production system focused on verified campus users.
Turned recommendation and pricing models into user-facing marketplace features.
takeaways: AI features matter most when they reduce a real user risk.
Vector search becomes valuable when it is integrated into a complete product journey.

title: Voice-ID & Neural Voice Cloning
subtitle: Speaker Authentication + Voice Synthesis
summary: An integrated audio system that authenticates enrolled speakers with ECAPA embeddings and generates cloned speech through a standardized multi-format pipeline.
problem: Voice applications need to distinguish enrolled users from unknown speakers while accepting inconsistent real-world audio formats.
approach: Generated SpeechBrain ECAPA speaker embeddings.
Calibrated cosine-similarity decisions rather than using an arbitrary threshold.
Standardized OGG, MP3, and WAV audio to 16 kHz.
Connected the identification stage with Coqui TTS voice cloning.
role: Designed the end-to-end audio preprocessing, speaker matching, threshold calibration, and synthesis workflow.
results: Established a custom decision threshold of 0.4814 for enrolled-vs-unknown queries.
Built a reusable multi-stage audio pipeline.
Combined authentication and generation in one coherent system.
takeaways: Calibration is as important as the embedding model.
Audio normalization prevents many failures before inference begins.

title: Cricket Ball & Bat Tracking
subtitle: Detection, Hit Events, Trajectory & Speed
summary: A YOLOv8-based vision pipeline for ball and bat detection, motion tracking, hit-event reasoning, trajectory reconstruction, and real-time speed estimation.
problem: A cricket ball is small, fast, frequently blurred, and often occluded, making reliable tracking and speed estimation difficult from ordinary video.
approach: Fine-tuned YOLOv8n for ball and bat bounding boxes.
Used tracking plus bounding-box interaction to identify hit events.
Applied optical-flow fallback for difficult frames.
Implemented Tomasi-Kanade-based 3D trajectory reconstruction for speed estimation.
role: Dataset preparation, YOLO training, event logic, tracking integration, trajectory work, and application-level visualization.
results: Produced ball-bat detections and tracked motion through video.
Connected detection output to hit-event and speed logic.
Built a practical computer-vision system rather than a standalone model notebook.
takeaways: Small-object detection needs temporal reasoning after the detector.
A useful sports system combines detection, tracking, geometry, and UI feedback.

title: Bank Customer Churn Prediction
subtitle: Classical ML + Neural Network Comparison
summary: A structured customer-risk modeling project comparing boosting pipelines with MLP and feed-forward neural-network approaches.
problem: Banks need interpretable and reproducible ways to identify customers who are likely to leave, so retention work can be targeted earlier.
approach: Cleaned and encoded customer attributes through reusable preprocessing pipelines.
Compared boosting algorithms with MLP and FNN models.
Evaluated models using classification metrics rather than accuracy alone.
Framed predictions in terms of retention decisions and customer-risk patterns.
role: End-to-end data preparation, model development, comparison, evaluation, and interpretation.
results: Built a repeatable model-comparison workflow.
Demonstrated both classical and neural approaches on the same business problem.
Created a portfolio-ready example of structured tabular ML.
takeaways: The best churn model must be judged with business-relevant errors.
Strong preprocessing often matters more than increasing neural-network depth.

title: Cobot Visuomotor Dataset Pipeline
subtitle: Video-Sensor Synchronization for Imitation Learning
summary: An automated pipeline that trims inactive robot data, synchronizes video frames with timestamps, and produces image-to-joint targets for cobot imitation learning.
problem: Raw cobot logs and video are not immediately trainable: movement must be isolated, frames must align with sensor time, and every image needs a consistent joint-angle target.
approach: Detected the last meaningful six-joint movement and trimmed inactive data.
Mapped every retained timestamp to its exact video frame.
Extracted synchronized images at 10 FPS.
Compiled a JSON dataset containing image path, timestamp, and six target joint angles.
role: Designed and implemented the complete data-cleaning, synchronization, extraction, and dataset-building workflow.
results: Generated 76 synchronized image-joint samples.
Covered timestamps from 0.0 to 7.5 seconds.
Produced a cross-platform JSON manifest ready for visuomotor learning experiments.
takeaways: Reliable synchronization is the core of multimodal robotics data.
A dataset pipeline should validate one-to-one correspondence before model training.

title: Texture Statistics vs Diffusion Features
subtitle: Heeger-Bergen, Wavelets & U-Net Analysis
summary: A research implementation comparing fixed multiscale texture statistics with learned diffusion U-Net representations and tracking statistical convergence during denoising.
problem: Diffusion models generate convincing textures, but it is unclear how their learned features relate to classical multiscale filter banks and when generated images recover the statistics of the original texture.
approach: Implemented steerable-pyramid decomposition and subband statistics.
Compared learned U-Net filters with classical multiscale filters in the frequency domain.
Tracked Wasserstein distances across denoising stages.
Tested a hybrid workflow where a classical statistical draft is refined by diffusion.
role: Research design, Python implementation, statistical analysis, visualization, tests, and interpretation of expected-vs-observed behavior.
results: Produced filter-comparison, statistical-evolution, and hybrid-synthesis outputs.
Built a reproducible multi-phase codebase with tests.
Connected classical texture theory to modern generative-model representations.
takeaways: Classical statistics and learned representations answer different questions.
A strong research result reports where the expected coarse-to-fine pattern holds and where it does not.

title: Air Pollution Prediction & Anomaly Detection
subtitle: Regression Benchmark + Isolation Forest
summary: An end-to-end notebook comparing six regression models for AQI prediction and adding unsupervised anomaly detection for unusual pollutant combinations.
problem: Global air-quality records require cleaning, comparison across multiple regressors, and a way to surface unusual observations beyond standard prediction metrics.
approach: Performed EDA, missing-value handling, outlier inspection, and feature preparation.
Benchmarked Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and SVR.
Used cross-validation alongside hold-out metrics.
Applied Isolation Forest to detect anomalous pollutant profiles.
role: Complete notebook implementation, model benchmarking, anomaly analysis, output export, and result interpretation.
results: Processed 23,463 source records.
Best recorded Gradient Boosting result: R2 0.9989 and RMSE 1.8947.
Flagged 1,174 rows as anomalies, approximately 5% of evaluated records.
takeaways: Very high AQI scores require leakage-aware interpretation because pollutant AQI components are closely related to the target.
Benchmark tables should include speed and cross-validation, not only the best hold-out score.

title: Python Point-of-Sale Desktop App
subtitle: Inventory, Receipts, Sales Logs & Windows Packaging
summary: A complete desktop POS workflow using an Excel product database, barcode lookup, stock updates, PDF receipts, daily sales logs, and a PyInstaller Windows executable.
problem: A small retail shop needs a simple offline system for products, billing, stock control, customer change, receipts, and daily records without operating a complex server.
approach: Created a barcode-based shopping cart and quantity workflow.
Loaded and updated inventory through Excel.
Generated formatted PDF receipts with ReportLab.
Logged daily sales to Excel and packaged the full app with PyInstaller.
role: Application logic, data access, cart behavior, stock validation, receipt design, logging, and Windows packaging.
results: Produced a directly runnable Windows executable.
Implemented stock-safe checkout, discounts, cash received, and change.
Generated persistent PDF receipts and daily Excel sales records.
takeaways: Deployment includes packaging, paths, and file permissions - not only application code.
Offline-first software can be the right architecture for a small business.

title: HexaQuote
subtitle: AI Voice-to-Quote React Native Platform
summary: A tradesperson records a job description; Whisper transcribes it, Llama structures the costs, Supabase stores the quote, and FastAPI returns a professional PDF for sharing.
problem: Tradespeople often create estimates manually after a site visit, losing time converting spoken notes into structured, professional quotes.
approach: Built an Expo/React Native frontend and FastAPI backend communicating over HTTP.
Used Groq Whisper for transcription and Llama 3.1 for strict JSON extraction.
Stored quotes in Supabase and generated PDFs with fpdf2.
Added platform-aware uploads, recent-quote history, offline queues, and automatic synchronization.
role: End-to-end product design, AI orchestration, backend APIs, mobile integration, database layer, PDF generation, and resilience behavior.
results: Converted voice notes into validated quote objects and shareable PDFs.
Separated frontend on port 8081 from backend on port 8000.
Implemented offline recording queues and auto-sync when connectivity returns.
takeaways: LLM output must be validated through a strict schema.
Mobile networking and offline behavior are product requirements, not edge cases.

title: Weighted YOLO
subtitle: Unified Multi-Generation Detection Architecture
summary: A proposed detector that studies YOLO evolution and combines weighted multi-scale fusion, modern CSP blocks, training-only gradient modules, and an end-to-end NMS-free head.
problem: YOLO generations introduce useful ideas independently, but a controlled study is needed to test which combinations improve the speed-accuracy trade-off and small-object detection.
approach: Reviewed modules introduced across YOLOv4/v5/v8/v9/v10/YOLO11 and later designs.
Designed a CSP-C3k2 backbone with SPPF, attention, and optional P2/P6 scales.
Replaced equal feature merging with learnable weighted PAN-FPN fusion.
Planned a one-to-many training head and one-to-one NMS-free inference path with ablations.
role: Architecture research, module comparison, implementation planning, weighted-fusion experiments, logging diagnosis, and ablation design.
results: Produced a complete architecture and part-by-part technical explanation.
Implemented learnable weighted neck fusion in matched experiments.
Maintained research-safe claims: the unified model remains experimental until longer ablations establish superiority.
takeaways: A novel architecture claim requires matched baselines and repeated ablations.
Training-only modules should improve optimization without increasing inference cost.

title: Explainable Brain Stimulation-Response AI
subtitle: 3D fMRI Transfer Learning + Multimodal Decision Support
summary: A leakage-aware multimodal framework combining pretrained 3D fMRI representations, stimulation/electrode metadata, uncertainty, visual interpretation, and grounded report generation.
problem: The epilepsy dataset contains only 159 CNN-compatible runs from 26 subjects, making random-initialization 3D CNN training unreliable and requiring strict subject-wise evaluation.
approach: Pretrained a residual 3D autoencoder on 6,562 BrainPedia statistical maps.
Continued self-supervised pretraining on 17,797 HCP task-fMRI maps from 787 subjects.
Fine-tuned a 64-dimensional encoder on Low/Moderate/High pseudo-labels using LOSO.
Integrated fMRI evidence with stimulation/electrode metadata, uncertainty, explainability, VLM interpretation, and grounded LLM reporting.
role: Research pipeline design, preprocessing, transfer learning, subject-wise validation, fusion, uncertainty, explainability, and reporting architecture.
results: Best documented subject-wise result: approximately 41.82% balanced accuracy and 42.05% macro-F1.
Established a 6,562 -> 17,797 -> 159 transfer-learning story.
Built an end-to-end research decision-support framework rather than claiming clinical validation.
takeaways: Subject-wise evaluation is mandatory when multiple runs come from the same person.
Pseudo-label uncertainty can be more important than simply making the CNN larger.

title: FG-KVQ
subtitle: Factorized Gated KV-Cache Quantization
summary: A preventive KV-cache quantization idea that separates Key magnitude into a compact gate and stores normalized Key content in low-bit form before cache insertion.
problem: Key vectors can contain extreme outlier channels that cause large low-bit quantization error; most existing methods react after outliers appear.
approach: Computed a compact scalar gate per token/head or RoPE group.
Normalized Key content before low-bit storage.
Restored the scale during attention while preserving RoPE geometry in full precision.
Designed comparisons against FP16, naive INT4, KIVI-style, and KVQuant-style baselines.
role: Novelty formulation, mathematical design, Hugging Face attention patching, cache capture, tensor reconstruction, metrics planning, and ablation design.
results: Successfully patched and captured K/V across 22 transformer layers.
Recorded a 41-token sequence with reconstructed K/V tensors.
Measured 0.0034 MB gate storage within a 0.4852 MB side-cache prototype.
takeaways: The decisive metric is attention-logit preservation, not Key MSE alone.
Current evidence proves the prototype mechanism, not superiority over mature baselines.
